pages.text: That morning, the river turned muddy yellow. Mom looked at it. "An earthy-colored river means rain is coming."
Laundry, baskets, and a straw mat lay in the yard. Raju wanted everything inside before rain. "I'll do it all!"
Mina offered a hand. Raju shook their head. "You two just sit."
Raju walked with arms full of baskets and the mat, unable to see their feet.
Raju crossed the yard again and again. Sweat dotted their forehead.
Laundry, baskets, and the mat still remained outside, soaked. Raju watched from under the roof.
Mom stood beside Raju. "Carrying alone was hard. Next time, ask your younger siblings, too."
The next day, the river grew cloudy again. Raju called the others. "Together this time!"
All three ran with an armful each. The yard was empty. Only then did raindrops fall.
